To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
COUP-TII is involved in the regulation of cell-type specific gene expression by binding to regulatory elements in a cell type-specific manner.
COUP-TII binds to regulatory elements that are marked with active histone modifications and co-bound by master TFs in a cell-type specific manner.
COUP-TII modulates cell-type specific genetic programmes by interacting with master transcription factors in a cell-type specific manner and with CTCF in a non-specific manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the cistrome, genomic contexts and the role of COUP TFII as a modulator of the cell-type specific genetic programs.
understanding the role of the transcription factor COUP-TF-II in the cell type-specific regulation of gene expression.
the role of the nuclear receptor COUP-TF-II in the transcriptional regulatory networks in different cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
COUP-TFI is a modulator for master transcription factors and CTCF in a cell-type specific manner.
COUP-TFI is a modulator in the cell-type-specific transcriptional program based on genomic localization.
COUP-TII is a modulating factor for cell-type-specific transcriptional programs based on genomic maps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
COUP-TFs are modulators of cell-type-specific transcription programs based on genomic localisation maps.
COUP-TFIIs binding sites are cell-type specific, and COUP-TFIs role in transcriptional regulation is modulated by its co-bound TFs.

COUP-TFIIs role in the cell type specific transcriptional programs is mediated by its co-localisation with master TFs in the active enhancer regions and with CTCF in the active promoter regions, while the angiogenic role of VEGFA is mediated by its long-range looping in the cell type-independent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
COUP-TII is involved in the transcriptional programs by co-localising with master transcription factors in a cell-type-specific manner.
COUP-TFs regulate the transcriptional program of cancer cells by interacting with master TFs and/or CTCF.
COUP-TFIIs binding to DNA is highly dependent on the cellular environment and that its binding is associated with cell-type specific master TFs.
